workflows.name: Contingent Labor Strategy & Workforce Category Planning

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "headcount equivalents by location/shift, seasonality" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approves strategy, sourcing model per category, authority for…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-523 (ensure controlled execution — Contingent Workforce Strategy, Sourcing & Compliance (PA-98.1).)
- operational: ratio guardrails (W3230); operational: make-vs-buy discipline
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-reliance risk**: Excessive contingent dependency signals misclassification exposure and erodes service quality; mitigated by ratio guardrails (W3230)
- **Strategic-misalignment risk**: Outsourcing a core capability loses control; mitigated by make-vs-buy discipline
System Touchpoints: - Workforce planning (links to VS-19.3); procurement/category (links to VS-34); FP&A (links to VS-17.4)

steps.activity: Contingent Workforce Mgr/HR (links to VS-19.3) assess demand by category: which functions are core (employee) vs non-core (contingent/outsource), headcount equivalents by location/shift, seasonality (Christmas promodizers per W555 context), peak/event demand (store openings VS-37, inventory counts); define make-vs-buy (employee vs contractor vs outsourced function)

Finance/Procurement (links to VS-34) build category cost model: fully-loaded employee cost vs contingent rate vs outsourced-function price; total-cost-of-ownership incl. management overhead, compliance, and risk premium; size addressable spend

Executive committee (CHRO/COO/CFO) approves strategy, sourcing model per category, authority for insource/outsource transitions (W3231), and contingency-to-regular ratio guardrails (W3230); integrate to VS-33 workforce plan and VS-19 hiring plan

workflows.name: DOLE D.O. 174 Labor-Only Contracting Compliance & Contract Structuring

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "Labor Compliance/Legal structure each contract to be legitimate job-contracting" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System continuous audit of "audit rights, recordkeeping, right-to-direct-reserved-to-contractor clause" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-test of "Labor Compliance maintain contracting-risk register and train operations supervisors" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: structuring discipline, four-fold-test training, and audit; operational: remittance verification (W3210/W3226) and indemnity
Pain Points / Risks: - **Labor-only finding risk**: DOLE/NLRC deems arrangement labor-only → workers become BuildRight employees with backwages, benefits, regularization; mitigated by structuring discipline, four-fold-test training, and audit
- **Solidary-liability risk**: BuildRight jointly liable for agency's unpaid wages/benefits; mitigated by remittance verification (W3210/W3226) and indemnity
System Touchpoints: - Contract/CMS (links to VS-22/VS-88); compliance register (links to VS-22); risk register (links to VS-21.2)
Time Estimate: - 1–2 weeks per contract structuring; ongoing training/audit

steps.activity: Labor Compliance/Legal structure each contract to be legitimate job-contracting (not labor-only): confirm contractor has substantial capital/investment (tools, equipment, premises), exercises direct control over its workers (hiring, firing, assignment, payroll, discipline), performs work distinct from BuildRight's core business where possible; avoid provisions implying employer-of-record (set hours, supervise day-to-day, integrate into BuildRight org)

Legal draft contract with compliance safeguards: principal-contractor relationship (not BuildRight–worker), contractor warrants DOLE/SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG/13th-month/wage compliance and indemnifies BuildRight, audit rights, recordkeeping, right-to-direct-reserved-to-contractor clause; align with VS-34 service-provider contract standards

Labor Compliance maintain contracting-risk register and train operations supervisors (Store Mgrs/DC Mgrs) on supervision boundaries — direct BuildRight supervisors must not assume employer functions (hire/fire/pay/direct-discipline) over contractor workers, which would convert them to BuildRight employees under the four-fold test; periodic audit (W3226)

fields.Participants: Contingent Workforce Mgr, User Dept, Procurement (links to VS-34), Legal, Agency

workflows.name: Statement of Work & Service Level Agreement Drafting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "checklist, promodizer targets" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "Define SLA and KPIs" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-communication of "communicate SLA to operations for performance management" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-523 (ensure controlled execution — Contingent Workforce Strategy, Sourcing & Compliance (PA-98.1).)
- operational: detailed SOW and change control; operational: balanced KPIs and audit (W3225)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scope-creep risk**: Undefined scope leads to disputes and extra cost; mitigated by detailed SOW and change control
- **SLA-gaming risk**: Contractor optimizes for metric over real quality; mitigated by balanced KPIs and audit (W3225)
System Touchpoints: - SOW/SLA repository; procurement (links to VS-34); performance scorecard (W3225)

steps.activity: User Dept/Contingent Workforce Mgr define scope of work and deliverables: headcount equivalents, coverage hours/shifts, work standards (security posts, cleaning checklist, promodizer targets), outputs/deliverables, exclusions, escalation path; avoid directing individual worker assignments (W3211 four-fold test)

Define SLA and KPIs: response/coverage, quality standards (audit score, defect rate), HSE performance (links to VS-24), attendance/reliability, customer/store satisfaction; measurement method, frequency, reporting; credit/penalty mechanism
Legal incorporate SOW/SLA into MSA (W3213); align to VS-34 service-provider standards; obtain sign-off; communicate SLA to operations for performance management (W3225)

fields.Participants: Procurement Mgr (links to VS-34), Contingent Workforce Mgr, Finance, Legal, Agency

workflows.name: Rate Negotiation, Benchmarking & Master Services Agreement

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "identify negotiation levers" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "discounts, payment terms" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System continuous audit of "audit rights, data privacy" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-523 (ensure controlled execution — Contingent Workforce Strategy, Sourcing & Compliance (PA-98.1).)
- operational: benchmarking to wage orders; operational: transparency on wage component
Pain Points / Risks: - **Wage-order-noncompliance risk**: Rate below mandated minimum triggers DOLE exposure (solidary); mitigated by benchmarking to wage orders
- **Margin-erosion risk**: Agency squeezes worker pay to protect margin → turnover/quality issues; mitigated by transparency on wage component
System Touchpoints: - Contract lifecycle/CMS (links to VS-34/VS-88); procurement (links to VS-34); privacy (links to VS-91)

steps.activity: Procurement/Finance benchmark rates to market: per-role/per-region market rates (security guard, cleaner, promodizer), wage-order compliance (Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board minimums per region — links to VS-76 multi-region), agency margin/loading norms; identify negotiation levers

Negotiate rate card, price-adjustment mechanism (wage-order pass-through, fuel for transport-linked), volume discounts, payment terms (links to VS-15); structure for compliance — no direct per-worker piece rates to BuildRight (worker paid by agency, not BuildRight)

Legal execute MSA: commercial terms, term/renewal, termination, compliance warranties, insurance/indemnity (W3214), audit rights, data privacy (links to VS-91 for worker personal data), dispute resolution; manage contract lifecycle (links to VS-34.2/W3274)

fields.Participants: Risk & Insurance Mgr (links to VS-26), Legal, Safety (links to VS-24), Procurement, Agency/Insurer

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "verify certificates of insurance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-register of "Manage claims involving contractors" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: COI verification and suspension-for-noncompliance; operational: category-specific limit setting
Pain Points / Risks: - **Uninsured-loss risk**: Contractor-caused damage with lapsed coverage shifts loss to BuildRight; mitigated by COI verification and suspension-for-noncompliance
- **Inadequate-limits risk**: Limits below exposure; mitigated by category-specific limit setting
System Touchpoints: - Insurance register/claims (links to VS-26); risk register (links to VS-21.2); contract/CMS (links to VS-34)

steps.activity: Risk & Insurance Mgr define risk-transfer requirements per category: contractor's general liability, employer's liability/workers' compensation (ECC coverage for their employees), professional indemnity (IT/engineering), third-party property damage, fidelity bond (for cash-handling security), motor (for delivery); set limits, deductibles, BuildRight as additional insured

Require and verify certificates of insurance (COI) before engagement and at renewal; verify authenticity with insurer; track expiry and renewals; enforce remediation for lapsed/non-compliant coverage (suspend engagement)

Manage claims involving contractors: incident response (W3228), coverage invocation, subrogation where BuildRight not at fault, deductible/allocation; lessons feed risk register (links to VS-21.2) and contract terms (W3213)

fields.Participants: Labor Compliance Mgr, Legal, HR (links to VS-84), Tax (links to VS-79), Contingent Workforce Mgr
fields.Trigger: New engagement; reclassification request; regulatory change; audit

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document classification rationale" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor via audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: four-fold-test discipline and proactive remediation; operational: documentation and tax review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Misclassification-liability risk**: NLRC regularization cases with back-wages and moral/exemplary damages; mitigated by four-fold-test discipline and proactive remediation
- **Tax-exposure risk**: BIR reclassification of contractors to employees; mitigated by documentation and tax review
System Touchpoints: - Classification/risk register (links to VS-21.2); legal matter (links to VS-100); payroll conversion (links to VS-19.2)

steps.activity: Labor Compliance/Legal apply the four-fold test (selection/engagement, payment of wages, power of dismissal, power of control) and economic-reality factors to each engagement and to individual-worker escalations (e.g., a long-tenured "contractor" worker seeking regularization); document classification rationale

Assess tax/ benefits exposure of misclassification: back wages, 13th month, SIL, premium pay, SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG, tax withholding; quantify potential liability and reserve (links to VS-100 legal loss contingency W3277); plan remediation (convert to regular per W3230, or restructure engagement)

Implement remediation and controls: convert confirmed employees to regular (W3230) with back-pay; restructure borderline engagements; train supervisors (W3211); update risk register and monitor via audit (W3226)

steps.activity: Contingent Workforce Mgr/Procurement evaluate renewal vs re-bid vs terminate: performance (W3225), compliance (W3226), market test, cost; obtain decision per authority matrix; for termination, document cause and notice per MSA

On non-renewal/termination: manage orderly transition — worker de-badging and access revocation (W3222), asset/tool/uniform recovery (W3222), final invoice reconciliation (W3221), continuity plan (replacement onboarding W3217 or insource W3231), no BuildRight severance obligation to contractor's workers (verify no conversion per W3215)
